name: Measure and report trading risk
summary: Each business day the independent commodity risk group, which reports to finance rather than to trading, values every open power, gas and environmental position at the previous day's market prices, works out the day's profit and loss, calculates value at risk and checks every exposure against the limits the board's committee approved. The result is a daily risk report for the trading director, the traders and the chief financial officer, with weekly and monthly reviews and month-end valuation entries for accounting. The work is slow and error-prone because forward prices for Alberta power are thin and must be checked by hand, new trades must be reconciled to exchange and broker records, and profit and loss differences must be agreed with traders before the report goes out.

baseline.org_archetype: An Alberta merchant generator of about 1,300 staff with a trading desk and a separate commodity risk and credit team of about 15 in finance.
baseline.notes: Covers the Alberta hedge book, customer contracts and the desk's short-term and proprietary trading positions held in one trading and risk system.

trigger: Trading closes for the day and the day's new trades and contracts are in the trading system.
end_state: The daily risk report is signed off and distributed, any limit breach is escalated with a remediation plan, and on weekly and month-end days the review package or valuation entries are delivered.

volume.seasonality: One report per business day; month-end and quarter-end days carry extra valuation and committee work.

evidence.note: VaR is calculated and reported on a daily basis (w2); business-day count by calendar.
Independent Risk Management group in w1 and daily VaR in w2; seven analysts in the organisation file, the rest of whose time goes to hedge accounting support, model work and ad hoc analysis.
Commodity risk team takes part in weekly reviews (w2); share estimated.
Traders resolve breaks and agree daily profit and loss.
Remediation plans for limit breaches.

roles.title: Executive vice-president (finance, operations, trading, legal, people, transition)

evidence.note: The EVP Finance and Trading and CFO chairs the Commodity Risk and Compliance Committee (w2).

systems.name: Energy trading and risk management system
Exchange and broker trading screens (NGX, ICE)

steps.name: Load end-of-day prices overnight
steps.description: After the close the trading and risk system loads exchange settlement prices from NGX and ICE and broker forward curves, and pulls the day's new deals into the overnight valuation batch.

error.defect_description: A curve feed fails or loads a stale file.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; overnight batch timing estimated.

steps.name: Hold Friday positions over the weekend
steps.description: Friday's positions and prices wait in the system until the risk analysts return on Monday morning; nothing is reported on weekends unless a large price move prompts a call to the risk manager.

evidence.note: Business-day reporting; weekend share is one day in five.

steps.name: Check weekend price moves
steps.description: On Monday the risk analyst first checks whether any weekend event, such as a pool price spike or an outage announcement, needs a note in the report before the normal run.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Validate forward curves
steps.description: The risk analyst compares the system's forward curves for Alberta power, AECO gas and emission credits with NGX settlements, independent broker quotes and the previous day, and flags points that are stale, illiquid or moved without reason.

error.defect_description: A bad curve point is accepted.

control.basis: Independent price verification by the risk group, not by traders

evidence.note: Independent risk management group in w1; method and times estimated.

steps.name: Correct curve points
steps.description: The risk analyst overrides the flagged points with a documented source, such as an interpolation between liquid months or the average of broker quotes, and records the override for audit.

error.defect_description: Override applied to the wrong month or product.

control.basis: Documented price overrides for fair value measurement of derivatives

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Reconcile new trades with exchange and broker records
steps.description: The risk analyst compares the previous day's new and amended deals in the trading system with the NGX and ICE trade reports and broker recaps, checking counts, volumes, prices and delivery periods.

control.basis: Trade validation by the independent risk group

evidence.note: Independent risk group in w1; times estimated.

steps.name: Trader explains or corrects deal break
steps.description: The term trader looks at each break, checks the screen history or calls the broker, and amends the deal or explains why the record differs.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; break rate and times estimated.

steps.name: Run valuation and position reports
steps.description: The trading and risk system revalues all positions on the validated curves and produces mark-to-market and position reports by book, tenor and commodity.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; run time estimated.

steps.name: Calculate and explain daily profit and loss
steps.description: The risk analyst splits the day's change in value into new deals, price moves, volume changes and settled deliveries, and writes a short explanation for each book whose result looks unusual.

error.defect_description: Change attributed to the wrong cause.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Agree daily profit and loss with the desk
steps.description: The traders compare the risk group's profit and loss with their own estimate and reply that they agree or raise a dispute about a price, a missing deal or a timing difference.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; dispute rate estimated.

steps.name: Investigate profit and loss dispute
steps.description: The risk analyst traces the disputed amount to a curve point, a deal attribute or a settlement, corrects the system if the desk is right, and records the outcome.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Run value at risk and stress tests
steps.description: The system calculates three-day value at risk at 95 percent confidence by the historical variance-covariance method for the trading books, gross margin at risk for the generation portfolio, and the periodic stress scenarios.

evidence.note: Daily three-day 95 percent historical variance/covariance VaR and periodic stress tests in w2.

steps.name: Review risk results
steps.description: The risk analyst compares today's value at risk, margin at risk and stress results with yesterday's, and traces any large jump to a position change, a curve move or a volatility update before the numbers are reported.

error.defect_description: Model or data error passed into the report.

evidence.note: VaR, gross margin at risk and tail risk measures in w1 and w2; review time estimated.

steps.name: Check exposures against limits
steps.description: The risk analyst compares each book's positions by tenor, value at risk, risk capital use and stop-loss with the approved limits and marks any breach or any limit above 90 percent use.

control.basis: Commodity and Financial Exposure Management policy approved by the board's Audit, Finance and Risk Committee

evidence.note: Risk capital and position limits (w1) and committee-approved policy (w2); breach rate estimated.

steps.name: Escalate limit breach
steps.description: The manager of commodity risk notifies the trader, the trading director and the chief financial officer of the breach, its size and cause, and asks for a remediation plan by a set time.

control.basis: Breach notification and escalation under the Commodity and Financial Exposure Management policy

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; escalation path assumed.

steps.name: Propose remediation for the breach
steps.description: The trading director decides whether to cut the position back inside the limit or to ask for a temporary limit increase and sends the plan to the risk manager.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; shares estimated.

steps.name: Approve temporary limit increase
steps.description: The chief financial officer, as chair of the commodity risk and compliance committee, approves or refuses a temporary limit increase with an expiry date.

control.basis: Limit changes approved above the trading line, by the committee chair

evidence.note: Commodity Risk and Compliance Committee chaired by the EVP Finance and Trading and CFO (w2); timing estimated.

steps.name: Draft daily risk report
steps.description: The risk analyst fills the daily report template with positions, mark-to-market, profit and loss, value at risk against limits, hedge percentages and any breaches with their status.

error.defect_description: Number copied from the wrong run.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Review and sign off report
steps.description: The manager of commodity risk reads the draft, checks the big movements and the breach section, and signs it off or sends it back for correction.

control.basis: Daily risk reporting by the independent risk group

evidence.note: VaR calculated and reported daily (w2); review time estimated.

steps.name: Distribute daily risk report
steps.description: The risk analyst publishes the report to the reporting site and emails it to the trading director, the traders, the chief financial officer and the credit team.

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Present at weekly trading risk review
steps.description: The manager of commodity risk walks the commercial managers and the chief financial officer through the week's positions, limit use, breaches and upcoming risks.
inputs: daily risk reports for the week

evidence.note: Weekly reviews by the commodity risk team, commercial managers and the EVP Finance and Trading and CFO (w2).

steps.name: Prepare month-end valuation entries
steps.description: On the last business day the risk analyst produces the month-end fair value of all derivatives by book and level of the fair value hierarchy and drafts the journal entries and support for accounting.

error.defect_description: Entry posted to the wrong account or book.

control.basis: Fair value support for derivatives under IFRS, reviewed by the external auditor

evidence.note: Tier C: author's estimate of common middle-office practice at an energy trading desk; times estimated.

steps.name: Prepare monthly committee package
steps.description: The manager of commodity risk assembles the monthly package for the commodity risk and compliance committee: limit use, breaches, value at risk back-testing, hedge levels and compliance items.

evidence.note: Monthly reviews by the Commodity Risk and Compliance Committee (w2); content and times estimated.

steps.name: Hold monthly commodity risk committee
steps.description: The committee, chaired by the chief financial officer with at least three senior managers, reviews the package, decides on standing limit changes to recommend and records actions.

control.basis: Commodity Risk and Compliance Committee oversight of trading risk and compliance

evidence.note: Committee chaired by the EVP Finance and Trading and CFO with at least three senior managers, meeting monthly (w2).

exceptions.name: Limit breach
exceptions.description: A position or VaR limit is breached; the risk manager escalates, the director proposes a plan and the CFO may approve a temporary increase.

exceptions.name: Deal break
exceptions.description: New deals in the system do not match exchange or broker records and must be corrected by the trader before valuation.

exceptions.name: Curve correction
exceptions.description: Stale or illiquid curve points are overridden with a documented source.

exceptions.name: Month-end
exceptions.description: Month-end valuation entries and the monthly committee package follow the daily report.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from trading close to distributed report
benchmarks.population: Daily risk report at an energy trading desk; Friday positions are reported on Monday

evidence.note: Author's estimate: report out around midday of the next business day; one report in five spans a weekend.

benchmarks.unit: percent confidence, three-day holding period, calculated daily

evidence.note: Historical variance/covariance method.
1 million CAD at end 2020.

pain_points.description: Alberta forward power trades thinly, so curve points beyond the prompt months must be checked and overridden by hand each day.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from Alberta market structure.

pain_points.description: Deal reconciliation to exchange and broker records is manual and breaks delay valuation until traders respond.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Profit and loss must be agreed with traders before the report goes out, and disputes take analyst time.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Month-end valuation and the committee package fall on the same days as the daily report.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Annual Information Form for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.1 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: Energy Marketing secures fuel supply and handles procurement of gas, transport and storage for the gas fleet; it trades power, natural gas and environmental products; the company regularly hedges portions of uncontracted merchant positions with physical and financial contracts; about 50 percent of capacity contracted in 2022 and 2023; an independent Risk Management group applies risk capital limits, value at risk, gross margin at risk, tail risk scenarios and position limits; the Pioneer Pipeline was integrated into NGTL and ATCO systems to supply Sundance and Keephills; long-term NGTL transportation agreements for 400 TJ per day; 1,282 employees at end 2021.

sources.title: TransAlta Corporation Management's Discussion and Analysis for the year ended December 31, 2021 (Exhibit 13.2 to Form 40-F)
sources.publisher: TransAlta Corporation via U.S. SEC EDGAR
sources.supports: VaR is calculated and reported daily, over a three-day holding period at 95 percent confidence, by the historical variance/covariance method, with periodic stress tests; VaR on proprietary trading was 2 million CAD at Dec. 31, 2021 (1 million in 2020); the Audit, Finance and Risk Committee approves the Commodity and Financial Exposure Management policies; trading risk is reviewed monthly by the Commodity Risk and Compliance Committee chaired by the EVP Finance and Trading and CFO and weekly by the commodity risk team, commercial managers and the CFO; Energy Trading Code of Conduct; about 78 percent of 2021 production under contracts and hedges; 70 percent of 2021 gas consumption contractually fixed or passed through; gas supply risk managed with at least two pipelines, firm delivery and supply contracts, gas hedges and monitoring of pipeline maintenance; 2022 Alberta hedges of 6,278 GWh at 75 CAD/MWh and 50 million GJ of gas at 2.75 CAD/GJ; credit limits by counterparty with collateral when exceeded.

assumptions: The daily report covers all books held in the trading and risk system: Alberta hedges, customer contracts and short-term trading.
Weekly and monthly reviews are modelled as branches after the daily report on one day in five and one day in 21.
Credit exposure and collateral are in fin-credit-collateral; this process only passes the report to the credit team.
No plant, vehicle or crew is held and no field work, weather or site access applies.
Term trader, trading director and the executive (CFO) take part but are not listed in the organisation file's process roles.

The simulation adds curve validation, deal reconciliation and profit and loss work in sequence although two or three analysts do them in parallel, so the simulated median (about 1.25 days) sits above the 1.0-day benchmark.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage x 1.40).
